pulls.title: Add independent equipment workspace with detailed mechanical inspection
pulls.body:
Smart Factory owns the equipment workspace, model/import validation, authentication, storage, Three.js renderer and local telemetry workflow. Native startup and inspection work from a frontend-only checkout with optional exchange disabled.

The MIT illustrative pump–coupling–motor reference has constructive bores, flange/mounting passages, mating seal faces, grooved bearing races/balls/cages, keyed coupling/guard, rotor/stator air gap, routed winding bundles, ventilation and terminal features. The reproducible revision-4 GLB is 186,236 triangles / 6,421,020 bytes. Its 87 selectable entries distinguish assemblies, individual parts and repeated sets; all 76 earlier template UUIDs remain. Generation enforces 83 clearance/contact/connectivity/interference checks.

Inspection supports whole/subassembly explosion, immediate scrubbing, exact restoration, hollow sections, hidden/clipped picking and focus, optional guides/labels, housing reveal and saved views. Selecting a component or receiving telemetry during animation now preserves the transition; reversal starts at the current pose. Imported emission/alpha and alpha masks survive inspection, invisible imported surfaces cannot affect picking/framing/caps, and empty saved selections restore after reload. HTTP telemetry rejection diagnostics are bounded and exclude invalid values.

Validation at functional source `ed7b0f3d4f792c00008c2fd750f8f1bcf50137a8`:
- 266 frontend tests / 34 files; 207 backend and 61 edge tests, including 99 independently owned provenance examples in each service.
- 26 general browser workflows passed / 7 expected opt-in skips; 5 standalone workflows passed / 1 public-only skip; Metal inspection and matched archived-v3 comparison passed.
- Fresh checkout, frozen installation, type check/build, model/BOM/AAS validation and both-theme desktop/narrow screenshots. Browser audit: zero peer requests; 3 blocked optional analytics attempts per viewport.
- Actual durable edge → Mosquitto → .NET 8 → authenticated Node preserved 20 generated simulated/replay samples during receiver outage and acknowledged all 20 after recovery.
- Apple M3 / ANGLE Metal desktop: all seven active stages have a 16.7 ms median; p95 is 18.3–33.3 ms. SwiftShader and emulated narrow results are labelled separately.
- [Functional-source CI passed](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend/actions/runs/40256170189); [pushed evidence-head CI also passed](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend/actions/runs/40320866253).

[Exact-source qualification, captures, logs and acceptance table](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend/blob/feat/native-equipment-monitoring/docs/equipment-evidence.md); [setup/auth/import instructions](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-iot-frontend/blob/feat/native-equipment-monitoring/docs/equipment-view.md).

Target physical-mobile performance, actual external-consumer interoperability, and physical phone/gateway/PLC/equipment qualification remain pending. The administrator journey explicitly verified pending-signup denial, chosen-role approval, rejection, effective Operator permissions, password-help review and mandatory temporary-password change.

The prior physical commissioning and broker-cutover evidence remains documented in `docs/pi-dht11-bench.md`. This update does not claim a new physical-device test or production deployment.

pulls.title: Fix registration approval, login retries and password recovery
pulls.body:
## Why
Repeated sign-in attempts could exhaust the lower password-recovery quota because both flows shared retry counters. Pending applicants also received generic credential failures, copied email whitespace was rejected before normalization, and administrators could not inspect reset-email delivery failures. A read-only demo administrator could block creation of the first individual administrator.

## Changes
- Separate persistent budgets for sign-in, registration, reset requests and token redemption; clear only the recovered account's sign-in counter after a successful reset.
- Normalize email before validation and lookup, show persistent form errors, and explain approval and duplicate-registration behavior accurately.
- Explain pending approval only after verifying the originally submitted password, without granting a session or revealing the state to incorrect credentials.
- Add bounded administrator-only recovery delivery metadata and a manual refresh control. Never expose reset tokens, links, hashes, encrypted payloads or raw delivery errors; distinguish provider acceptance from inbox receipt.
- Repair private first-administrator bootstrap when only shared demo admins exist. Preserve refusal for any existing individual admin, including disabled ones, and preserve existing passwords/activation rules with transactional auditing.
- Add real HTTP authentication lifecycle tests and extend the administrator browser journey through a chosen password and fresh sign-in.
- Qualify one continuous recovery through the packaged API, PostgreSQL queue, real C# worker, authenticated STARTTLS capture, actual emailed link, token redemption and new-password login through IdentityService. Keep the capture service private and bounded, and remove its container, network and certificate volume at teardown.
- Run the three isolated browser suites in parallel so the full pipeline completes within its job budgets. Preserve the required `Build and Test` check as an explicit aggregate; every existing test and release gate is retained. Wait for stable page snapshots and completed rejection dialogs in the browser assertions.

## Validation
- 130 authentication API/database cases passed across 10 suites against disposable PostgreSQL.
- 9 browser authentication UI tests passed.
- The [real administrator browser journey](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-frontend/actions/runs/41222172149/job/124598939298) passed registration, approval/rejection, login, administrator recovery, forced password change, logout and fresh chosen-password login. Its suite completed with 7 passed and 1 unrelated optional edge test skipped.
- Full TypeScript check and production Vite build passed.
- Companion [backend PR #13](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-backend/pull/13) adds actual authenticated STARTTLS transport coverage; all 39 reset-worker tests passed and its CI is green.
- 15 native SMTP fixture tests passed. The full packaged recovery, restart/rollback, security scan and cleanup passed [ARM64 qualification](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-frontend/actions/runs/41222172145) for `1d1046197f413cb0dc0db59c57af0deb035fe1cd`. The exact tested candidate and compatible rollback are retained in its `qualified-arm64-bundle` artifact.

- Final [Dashboard quality checks](https://github.com/DruHustle/smart-factory-frontend/actions/runs/41222172149) passed all 11 jobs. The database-backed suite passed 766 tests (1 skipped test); browser smoke passed all 27 with no retries. Production frontend build, documentation/deployment checks, build-output verification and dependency audit passed.

## Release boundaries
No production account, password, role, recipient policy or service configuration was changed. The live generic reset confirmation does not prove account existence or email receipt. A separate read-only diagnostic has been prepared for the installation owner's existing SSH connection to resolve the reported account's state and latest delivery result.

This PR includes API code and needs the qualified Oracle API/worker image installed for its backend fixes to take effect. Existing deployment gates, approval policy and source pins remain intact. ## Why
The first individual Administrator cannot depend on approval from an Administrator who has not been created yet. The current sign-in and registration screens do not make the private deployment setup step clear, which leaves the factory owner unsure how to gain access and approve later signups.

## Changes
- Explain private first-administrator setup on the sign-in and registration screens, without exposing whether an administrator exists or providing a public administrator-claim action.

- Scope incident lists, action queues and exports to named factories before ordering/limiting.

- Provide six clearly labelled recorded scenarios with consistent signal/calculation inputs and equipment/Assistant handoff.
